refusal.where: applying v1.7's 28 operations against verified v1.6 bytes, at depth 3; v1.8's and v1.9's operations were therefore never reached
refusal.errors: 26 of 28 operations refuse, every one with 'does not resolve against the predecessor': operation indices 0-4 and 7-27, all sets
refusal.theTwoThatDidNotError: operations 5 and 6 are adds ('/successorContextV17', '/findingIdentity'). Under the mis-parsed grammar each would have SUCCEEDED by inserting a literal top-level key named with the full slash string -- an invented contract, not the declared one. The loud refusal of this chain is therefore LUCK, not design: sets are guarded by the from-restatement and existence check; adds carry no guard against a mis-parsed path.

cause.measured: the r1 lineage declares operation paths in RFC 6901 JSON-Pointer form ('/positiveVectors/4/...'). Both instruments walk dotted paths only: STEP_RE, inherited from check-c2-v9.py, tokenises 'a.b[3].c'. A pointer path does not match that grammar, and path_steps does not refuse it -- it mis-tokenises the entire path into ONE step ('/version' -> ['/version']) because '/' is not an excluded character. No predecessor key equals that token, so every set refuses.
cause.theSharpEdge: path_steps' own docstring states 'Guessing at a malformed path is how a resolver invents a contract the artifact never declared' -- and for pointer paths the function does exactly what it warns against: it returns a confident wrong parse instead of None. The refusal branch ('path is not plainly resolvable') is unreachable for this entire dialect.
cause.class: this is the third instance of the §7.3 rider class 'a deliberate, reasonable authoring choice is unreadable to the consuming instrument': (1) array-token paths, refused silently, recorded 2026-08-10; (2) the v26 change-log false positive, recorded 2026-08-10; (3) JSON-Pointer paths, measured here -- sets refused loudly, adds mis-applied silently.
